subtype: Approach: learning from last year's trip and adjusting [Revision]
passage: Last year on the trip to the science park, my small bottle was empty by noon. My mouth felt like paper and I had to ask Hemant for sips, which made me feel bad. So this time I packed the big steel bottle. Amma said it was heavy, but I said I would rather be heavy than thirsty. I also told Hemant, "Bring a big one too, it gets really hot there." He laughed but agreed. At noon we sat in the shade, both bottles still half full, and I remembered last year and smiled. - Sonali

qa.q: Why did Sonali have to ask Hemant for sips last year?
qa.a: Sonali's small bottle was empty by noon.

qa.q: How did Sonali feel about asking Hemant for sips last year?
qa.a: Sonali felt bad and uncomfortable about it, and that memory pushed the change to a bigger bottle.

qa.q: What other approach could Sonali use to make sure water lasts through a hot day, and why?
qa.a: Sonali could ask the teacher where taps are on the route and top up there, so the day does not depend on one bottle.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Sonali's advice to bring a big bottle?
qa.a: He laughed, so it may seem a bit fussy at first, but at noon his bottle is half full too, which suggests the advice was sensible.

grounding: A child recalls being thirsty on last year's trip and changes the plan with a bigger bottle and a word to a friend.
